facts.raw_span: A man in his 60s with a history of hypertension and diabetes mellitus
who worked as a butcher and occasional hunter and had contact with hares and rabbits
presented with lesions on left hand evolving over 3 days
vesiculobullous lesions appeared on the dorsal aspect of his left hand and extended into the web space between the first and second fingers
the lesion extended to the palm and ventral aspect of the thumb with an eroded area on which pustules appeared
No fever or other systemic symptoms were present
Hemorrhagic bullous lesions on the dorsal aspect of left hand extending to web space between first and second fingers
Surface erosion with pustular lesions on palm and ventral aspect of thumb
Fungal culture was negative
bacterial culture showed Staphylococcus simulans
Polymerase chain reaction analysis for Erysipelothrix rhusiopathiae was negative
Initially hemorrhagic bullous lesions appeared

concepts.why: The patient's bacterial culture showed Staphylococcus simulans and presented with hemorrhagic bullous lesions on the left hand, which is consistent with a Staphylococcal skin infection.

The patient's occupation as a butcher and contact with hares and rabbits, along with the presentation of lesions on the left hand, are consistent with Erysipeloid, although the PCR analysis for Erysipelothrix rhusiopathiae was negative.
The patient's presentation of lesions on the left hand, including hemorrhagic bullous lesions and surface erosion with pustular lesions, is consistent with Cellulitis, a bacterial skin infection.

The patient's occupation as a butcher and contact with hares and rabbits, along with the presentation of lesions on the left hand, could be consistent with Cutaneous anthrax, although there is no direct evidence of Bacillus anthracis infection.
The patient's presentation of lesions on the left hand, including pustular lesions, is consistent with Impetigo, a highly contagious bacterial skin infection.
The patient's presentation of lesions on the left hand, including surface erosion with pustular lesions, could be consistent with Pyoderma gangrenosum, a rare skin condition.

The patient's presentation of lesions on the left hand, including hemorrhagic bullous lesions, could be consistent with a Streptococcal skin infection, although there is no direct evidence of Streptococcus pyogenes infection.
The patient's presentation of lesions on the left hand, including pustular lesions, is consistent with Ecthyma, a bacterial skin infection.

rationales.F02: Contact with hares and rabbits increases the likelihood of Erysipeloid.
rationales.F10: Presence of Staphylococcus simulans in bacterial culture strongly supports Staphylococcal skin infection.
rationales.F11: Negative PCR result for Erysipelothrix rhusiopathiae rules out Erysipeloid.
